statement.p: Consider the (approximate) unit vector \langle 0.99,-0.12 \rangle. Give another unit vector different from it, but still parallel to it.

solution.p: Vectors are parallel if they are scalar multiples of one another. If we multiply \langle 0.99,-0.12 \rangle by any scalar, it will change its length, making it no longer a unit vector, unless the scalar we choose is 1 or -1. Multiplying by 1 gives us the same vector again, but we were asked for a different one. Thus we must choose -1\cdot\langle 0.99,-0.12 \rangle, which is \langle -0.99,0.12 \rangle.
